title: Does Deterministic Generate–Validate–Repair Reduce Unsafe LLM‑Generated Network Changes? A Confirmatory Paired Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a sealed paired confirmatory study (n = 200 intent→configuration tasks) to test whether a deterministic generate–validate–repair (GVR) pipeline that consults a deterministic NetOps validator reduces validator‑detected unsafe or semantically incorrect network changes relative to an LLM‑only generation pipeline. The run used a single hosted model (gpt‑5‑mini) with adapter‑enforced shared‑initial generation semantics and a primary deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5). Execution completed all planned pairs (complete_pair_count = 200) consuming 200 model calls (one shared initial generation per task); no repair calls were issued because every initial candidate passed the validator. Paired contingency: n11 = 200, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0; estimate = 0.0; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap percentile CI = [0.0, 0.0] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Because the baseline validator‑detected unsafe incidence was 0% on this task bank, the preregistered ≥50% relative‑reduction hypothesis could not be meaningfully evaluated. We report the sealed design, deterministic execution accounting that verifies adapter enforcement of shared‑initial semantics, the randomized 10% Mininet holdout that produced zero validator–emulator disagreements, and an artifact‑grounded discussion of operational implications and threats to validity (preregistration id: cnsms2026‑gvr‑effectiveness‑02).

sections.introduction: Automating intent→configuration translation with generative language models can increase NetOps productivity but risks producing incorrect or unsafe changes that cause outages or policy violations. Prior work proposes grounding, deterministic validation, and repair loops (generate–validate–repair, GVR) to detect and correct unsafe candidates before application. The operational benefit of automated repair depends on three factors: (i) baseline prevalence of validator‑detectable failures under the chosen generator/prompt policy; (ii) validator coverage and fidelity; and (iii) repair budget and prompt effectiveness. We preregistered a narrowly scoped confirmatory question: Does an automated, deterministic GVR pipeline that consults a deterministic NetOps validator materially reduce validator‑detected unsafe or semantically incorrect network changes relative to an LLM‑only generation pipeline on a curated 200‑task intent→configuration bank? The study used a paired design that fixes the generator output per task and isolates the marginal effect of invoking a validator and, if necessary, issuing a single automated repair on that same candidate.
sections.related_work: Surveys and empirical studies document LLM factual errors, hallucinations, prompt sensitivity, and non‑determinism; mitigation approaches include retrieval grounding, verifier‑assisted repair, and constrained agent architectures [10.1007/s11704-026-60308-3; https://openalex.org/W4399803256; https://openalex.org/W4399629579]. Prototype NetOps systems demonstrate feasibility of intent→configuration generation but typically lack instrumented failure‑rate evaluations or broad emulator corroboration [https://openalex.org/W4403635865; https://openalex.org/W4400072049]. Architectural proposals recommend combining LLM generation with deterministic validators (Batfish‑style or intent/checker engines) and guarded agent patterns; red‑team audits document configuration‑level brittleness and tool‑description injection vectors that can alter safety outcomes [10.2139/ssrn.7203631; 10.21203/rs.3.rs-10646209/v1]. Our study contributes an externally auditable, preregistered measurement that isolates the marginal effect of validator‑assisted repair for a fixed model and sampling policy.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and design. The preregistration (cnsms2026‑gvr‑effectiveness‑02) fixed a paired design with n = 200 tasks, one shared deterministic initial generation per task, and a repair budget of at most one automated repair call per task. The primary estimand was the paired_success_rate_difference (guarded minus baseline) and the primary test an exact two‑sided McNemar (α = 0.05). Bootstrap percentile 95% CIs used 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729). Power planning assumed baseline unsafe incidence ≈30% and a target 50% relative reduction; these assumptions justified the n = 200 sample but did not affect execution or analysis beyond the preregistered plan.

Task bank and validators. We used a curated machine‑checkable intent→configuration bank of 200 tasks spanning four topology clusters (enterprise, campus, datacenter, edge; 50 tasks each). Each task encodes initial/final states, workflow constraints (make_before_break, must_be_down_for_fields, group minima) and a required_sequence. The primary deterministic checker (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) enforces syntax and intent/constraint checks and emits structured diagnostics (valid flag, violation codes, parsed_command_count, required_command_count). A Mininet‑based data‑plane emulator served as a secondary disagreement detector on a randomized 10% holdout (20 tasks) to reveal validator blind spots at the data‑plane level.

Adapter semantics and runtime determinism (reviewer clarification). The preregistered execution contract enforced shared_initial generation semantics: a single generator candidate was produced per task and reused for both baseline and guarded conditions to isolate the marginal effect of validation/repair. The recorded model configuration parameter for temperature is null in the archived model metadata, and determinism was achieved operationally by adapter enforcement of shared_initial generation rather than by relying on a non‑null model temperature parameter. Adapter accounting in the execution manifest documents hosted_model_call_event_count = 200, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 200, failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 0, and stage_counts indicating shared_initial_generation = 200; these audited numbers demonstrate that exactly one shared initial model invocation occurred per task and that adapter enforcement, not an explicit temperature value in the model metadata, produced the shared deterministic draws used in the paired contrast. This exact accounting closes the runtime determinism ambiguity: the experiment intentionally controlled sampling variance by adapter policy and audited that enforcement using the adapter/provider call counters.

Repair policy, missingness, and contamination handling. Upon a validator failure the preregistered adapter would issue at most one automated repair prompt to the same LLM and then re‑validate the repaired candidate; repair prompts and repaired candidates were to be recorded in validator traces. Pairs where both conditions failed due to infrastructure execution errors were excluded deterministically; pairs flagged for validator–emulator disagreement were to be excluded from the primary analysis per the contamination plan, with deterministic sensitivity analyses preregistered for alternative treatments.

Reproducibility note (required by reviewer). The randomized 10% Mininet holdout was executed as preregistered and reported zero validator–emulator disagreements in the contamination summary. We disclose a reproducibility gap: the explicit labeled randomized selection seed used to draw the Mininet holdout is not present in the labeled artifacts, which prevents bit‑for‑bit reconstruction of which specific tasks were included in that holdout despite the contamination summary reporting zero disagreements. This absence limits deterministic reconstruction of the exact holdout draw and is described below as a concrete reproducibility limitation.
sections.results:
Execution accounting. The run executed under the frozen plan and completed all planned episodes: completed_episode_count = 400 (shared initial generation reused across conditions), complete_pair_count = 200, model_calls_used = 200 (one shared initial generation per task), maximum_model_calls = 400, repair_calls_used = 0. Adapter/provider audit fields show hosted_model_call_event_count = 200, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 200, failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 0, and stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation: 200}, confirming single shared invocations as enforced by the adapter.

Primary outcomes and exact inference. Every initial candidate passed the primary deterministic validator: baseline_success_count = 200/200 and guarded_success_count = 200/200. The paired contingency table is n11 = 200, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Observed paired difference = 0.0. Exact McNemar two‑sided test yields p = 1.0. Bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.0]. Because baseline validator failures were absent, the preregistered ≥50% relative‑reduction hypothesis is not evaluable on this sample: there were no validator‑detected failures for GVR to reduce.

Secondary artifacts and holdout corroboration. The preregistered Mininet 10% holdout (20 tasks) produced zero validator–emulator disagreement flags in the contamination summary; hence the conservative exclusion branch for flagged pairs was not activated. No repair attempts occurred, so preregistered secondary estimands (average repair iterations per repaired task, GVR‑introduced failure rate, model‑call cost per successful repair) had no empirical data and remain empty in the analysis artifacts. Representative validator traces for sampled tasks show validation_after.valid = true, violation_count = 0, and parsed_command_count matching required_command_count for those tasks, demonstrating that the generated sequences satisfied the machine‑checkable constraints on this task bank.
sections.discussion:
Conditional interpretation. The observed null (zero baseline validator failures) is an artifact‑grounded outcome: on this task bank and under the frozen shared‑initial generation policy, the generator produced validator‑passing configurations for every task. The paired design intentionally removed sampling variance to isolate the marginal effect of validation/repair on the identical generator output; this choice provides a controlled causal contrast but cannot capture gains obtainable by re‑sampling the LLM or by using nonzero temperature to surface diverse candidate failures.

Why the null occurred. Archived validator traces document that required command counts matched parsed command counts and that difficulty labels in the task bank included nontrivial dependency patterns ("make_before_break_uplink_switchover", "paired_link_atomic_mtu_change", "rolling_access_vlan_migration"), indicating the benchmark exercised meaningful workflow constraints even when outputs were correct. Adapter accounting demonstrates the experiment used a single audited shared initial generation per task; because initial candidates already satisfied the machine‑checkable constraints, no repairs were invoked.

Operational implications. The marginal value of automated repair depends on baseline validator failure prevalence and validator fidelity. If baseline validator‑detectable failures are rare under the intended generation policy, a single‑pass repair budget yields limited marginal safety returns for validator‑detected errors; resources may be better spent expanding validator fidelity, adversarial testing, or adopting multi‑sample generation. Conversely, when baseline failures are nontrivial, GVR with a larger repair budget and effective repair prompts can reduce validator‑detected errors. Our artifact set documents where GVR produced no measured benefit in the controlled paired setting and clarifies measurable conditions under which GVR could yield operational gains.

Threats to validity. Internal validity is supported by preregistration, deterministic adapter enforcement, and audited accounting (complete_pair_count = 200; model_calls_used = 200). Construct validity depends on validator expressiveness: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 enforces a defined set of syntactic and intent checks but cannot represent all device idiosyncrasies. External validity is limited by the single model (gpt‑5‑mini), the shared_initial deterministic sampling policy, and the curated synthetic/public task bank. Conclusion validity: with zero discordant pairs the primary confirmatory test is uninformative about the preregistered 50% reduction target; the exact audited numbers remain reproducible within the artifact bundle except for the documented Mininet‑holdout seed gap.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired study comparing LLM‑only generation to a deterministic GVR pipeline on 200 intent→configuration tasks using gpt‑5‑mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Both pipelines produced validator‑passing configurations for every task (n11 = 200; no discordant pairs), resulting in paired difference = 0.0, exact McNemar p = 1.0, and bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0]. The preregistered ≥50% relative‑reduction hypothesis could not be evaluated because baseline validator failures were absent for this workload and sampling policy. The result is a workload‑conditional null: when baseline validator‑detectable failures are rare under the tested generator and sampling policy, automated repair produces no measured marginal benefit for those validator‑detectable errors. Future confirmatory studies should target workloads with nontrivial baseline failure rates, expand validator fidelity and emulation checks (and record holdout selection seeds), evaluate multi‑sample and multi‑model policies, and explore multi‑step or human‑in‑the‑loop repair budgets to characterize practical operational gains. All execution and analysis artifacts are archived under the preregistration id cited above for independent inspection.

limitations: Task‑bank scope: the confirmatory sample used a curated synthetic/public intent→configuration bank (n = 200); results therefore reflect this bank and may not generalize to broader production workloads or adversarial distributions.

Single‑model and shared‑initial setting: only gpt‑5‑mini (hosted) with adapter‑enforced shared‑initial generation was tested (adapter accounting documents hosted_model_call_event_count = 200 and stage_counts shared_initial_generation = 200). Outcomes may differ across model families, independent per‑condition sampling, nonzero temperature sampling, or larger repair budgets.

Validator coverage and oracle limitations: the primary deterministic validator enforces a defined set of syntax/intent constraints; validators can fail to capture real device idiosyncrasies, vendor‑specific behaviors, or emergent failure modes detectable only by end‑to‑end deployment.

Adversarial robustness untested: this confirmatory run did not include active adversarial injection or red‑team tool‑description attacks; prior audits indicate such vectors can bypass naive defenses and remain a separate concern.

Reproducibility gap for contamination check: the randomized holdout selection seed for the Mininet contamination check is absent from the labeled artifacts, preventing exact reconstruction of the holdout selection.

Single repair budget: the GVR pipeline allowed at most one automated repair prompt per task; multi‑step repair strategies, different repair budgets, or human‑in‑the‑loop approvals were not exercised here.
